paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Millions die early from air pollution each year. Air pollution costs the global economy more than $5 trillion annually in welfare costs, with the most serious 26 occurring in the developing world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 每年有数百万人因空气污染而提前死亡。空气污染每年给全球经济造成超过 5 万亿美元的福利成本，其中发展中国家受到的损失最为严重。

paragraphs.sourceText: The figures include a number of costs 27 with air pollution. Lost income alone amounts to $225 billion a year.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些数字包括一些与空气污染相关的成本。仅收入损失一年就达 2250 亿美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: The report includes both indoor and outdoor air pollution. Indoor pollution, which includes 28 like home heating and cooking, has remained 29 over the past several decades despite advances in the area. Levels of outdoor pollution have grown rapidly along with rapid growth in industry and transportation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该报告包括室内和室外空气污染。尽管室内污染（包括家庭取暖和烹饪等来源）在过去几十年中一直保持不变，尽管该领域取得了进步。随着工业和交通运输的快速发展，室外污染水平也迅速增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: Director of Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation Chris Murray 30 it as an “urgent call to action.”“One of the risk factors for premature deaths is the air we breathe, over which individuals have little 31 ,”he said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 健康指标与评估研究所所长克里斯·默里（Chris Murray）将其描述为“紧急行动呼吁”。“过早死亡的风险因素之一是我们呼吸的空气，而个人对此几乎无法控制，”他说。

paragraphs.sourceText: The effects of air pollution are worst in the developing world, where in some places lost-labor income 32 nearly 1% of GDP. Around 9 in 10 people in low-and middle-income countries live in places where they 33 experience dangerous levels of outdoor air pollution.
paragraphs.translationZh: 空气污染对发展中国家的影响最为严重，一些地方的劳动力收入损失相当于 GDP 的近 1%。在低收入和中等收入国家，大约十分之九的人生活在经常遭受危险水平室外空气污染的地方。

paragraphs.sourceText: But the problem is not limited 34 to the developing world. Thousands die prematurely in the U.S. as a result of related illnesses. In many European countries, where diesel(柴油) 35 have become more common in recent years, that number reaches tens of thousands.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但问题不仅仅限于发展中国家。在美国，数千人因相关疾病过早死亡。在许多欧洲国家，柴油车近年来变得越来越普遍，这一数字达到数万辆。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. Food-as-Medicine Movement Is Witnessing Progress
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应字母来回答问题。食品作为药物运动正在见证进展

paragraphs.sourceText: A. Several times a month, you can find a doctor in the aisles of Ralph’s market in Huntington Beach, California, wearing a white coat and helping people learn about food. On one recent day, this doctor was Daniel Nadeau, wandering the cereal aisle with Allison Scott, giving her some idea on how to feed kids who persistently avoid anything that is healthy. “Have you thought about trying fresh juices in the morning?” he asks her. “The frozen oranges and apples are a little cheaper, and fruits are really good for the brain. Juices are quick and easy to prepare, you can take the frozen fruit out the night before and have it ready the next morning.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：每个月都有几次，你可以在加利福尼亚州亨廷顿海滩的拉尔夫市场的过道里找到一位医生，他穿着白大褂，帮助人们了解食物。最近的一天，丹尼尔·纳多（Daniel Nadeau）医生和艾莉森·斯科特（Allison Scott）一起在麦片货架上徘徊，向她提供了一些关于如何喂养那些一直回避任何健康食品的孩子的想法。 “你有没有想过早上尝试新鲜果汁？”他问她。 “冷冻橙子和苹果便宜一点，水果对大脑确实有好处。果汁制作起来又快又容易，你可以在前一天晚上把冷冻水果拿出来，第二天早上就可以准备好了。”

paragraphs.sourceText: B. Scott is delighted to get food advice from a physician who is program director of the nearby Mary and Dick Allen Diabetes Center, part of the St. Joseph Hoag Health alliance. The center’s ‘Shop with Your Doc’ program sends doctors to the grocery store to meet with any patients who sign up for the service, plus any other shoppers who happen to be around with questions.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. Scott 很高兴从一位医生那里得到饮食建议，这位医生是附近玛丽和迪克艾伦糖尿病中心的项目主任，该中心是圣约瑟夫霍格健康联盟的一部分。该中心的“与医生一起购物”计划会派医生到杂货店会见所有报名参加该服务的患者，以及任何其他碰巧有问题的购物者。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. Nadeau notices the pre-made macaroni (通心粉)-and-cheese boxes in Scott’s shopping cart and suggests she switch to whole grain macaroni and real cheese. “So I’d have to make it?”she asks, her enthusiasm fading at the thought of how long that might take, just to have her kids reject it. “I’m not sure they’d eat it. They just won’t eat it.”
paragraphs.translationZh: C. Nadeau 注意到 Scott 购物车中的预制通心粉和奶酪盒，建议她改用全麦通心粉和真正的奶酪。 “所以我必须成功吗？”她问道，一想到这可能需要多长时间，她的热情就消退了，只是为了让她的孩子们拒绝。 “我不确定他们会吃它。他们就是不吃。”

paragraphs.sourceText: D. Nadeau says sugar and processed foods are big contributors to the rising diabetes rates among children. “In America, over 50 percent of our food is processed food,” Nadeau tells her. “And only 5 percent of our food is plant-based food. I think we should try to reverse that.” Scott agrees to try more fruit juices for the kids and to make real macaroni and cheese. Score one point for the doctor, zero for diabetes.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. Nadeau 说，糖和加工食品是导致儿童糖尿病发病率上升的主要原因。 “在美国，超过 50% 的食物都是加工食品，”纳多告诉她。 “我们的食物中只有 5% 是植物性食物。我认为我们应该尝试扭转这一局面。”斯科特同意为孩子们尝试更多果汁，并制作真正的通心粉和奶酪。医生得一分，糖尿病得零分。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. Nadeau is part of a small revolution developing across California. The food-as-medicine movement has been around for decades, but it’s making progress as physicians and medical institutions make food a formal part of treatment, rather than relying solely on medications (药物). By prescribing nutritional changes or launching programs such as ‘Shop with your Doc’, they are trying to prevent, limit or even reverse disease by changing what patients eat. “There’s no question people can take things a long way toward reversing diabetes, reversing high blood pressure, even preventing cancer by food choices,” Nadeau says.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. Nadeau 是加州正在掀起的一场小革命的一部分。食物即药物运动已经存在了几十年，但随着医生和医疗机构将食物作为治疗的正式一部分，而不是仅仅依赖药物，它正在取得进展。通过改变营养处方或启动“与医生一起购物”等计划，他们试图通过改变患者的饮食来预防、限制甚至逆转疾病。纳多说：“毫无疑问，人们可以通过选择食物来长期逆转糖尿病、高血压，甚至预防癌症。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F. In the big picture, says Dr. Richard Afable, CEO and president of ST. Joseph Hoag Health, medical institutions across the state are starting to make a philosophical switch to becoming a health organization, not just a health care organization. That feeling echoes the beliefs of the Therapeutic Food Pantry program at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital, which completed its pilot phase and is about to expand on an ongoing basis to five clinic sites throughout the city. The program will offer patients several bags of food prescribed for their condition, along with intensive training in how to cook it. “We really want to link food and medicine, and not just give away food,” says Dr. Rita Nguyen, the hospital’s medical director of Healthy Food Initiatives. “We want people to understand what they’re eating, how to prepare it, the role food plays in their lives.”
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 从大局来看，ST 首席执行官兼总裁 Richard Afable 博士说。 Joseph Hoag Health 表示，全州的医疗机构正在开始转变理念，成为一个健康组织，而不仅仅是一个医疗保健组织。这种感觉与扎克伯格旧金山总医院的治疗食品储藏室计划的信念相呼应，该计划已完成试点阶段，并将持续扩展到全市的五个诊所站点。该计划将为患者提供几袋适合其病情的食物，并提供如何烹饪的强化培训。 “我们真的希望将食物和药物联系起来，而不仅仅是赠送食物，”该医院健康食品倡议医疗主任 Rita Nguyen 博士说。 “我们希望人们了解他们在吃什么、如何准备食物以及食物在他们的生活中扮演的角色。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G. In Southern California, Loma Linda University School of Medicine is offering specialized training for its resident physicians in Lifestyle Medicine — that is a formal specialty in using food to treat disease. Research findings increasingly show the power of food to treat or reverse diseases, but that does not mean that diet alone is always the solution, or that every illness can benefit substantially from dietary changes. Nonetheless, physicians say that they look at the collective data and a clear picture emerges: that the salt, sugar, fat and processed foods in the American diet contribute to the nation’s high rates of obesity, diabetes and heart disease. According to the World Health Organization, 80 percent of deaths from heart disease and stroke are caused by high blood pressure, tobacco use, elevated cholesterol and low consumption of fruits and vegetables.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 在南加州，洛马琳达大学医学院正在为其住院医生提供生活方式医学方面的专门培训——这是使用食物治疗疾病的正式专业。研究结果越来越多地显示食物治疗或逆转疾病的力量，但这并不意味着饮食永远是解决方案，或者每种疾病都可以从饮食改变中受益匪浅。尽管如此，医生们表示，在查看集体数据后，我们可以清楚地看到：美国饮食中的盐、糖、脂肪和加工食品导致了美国肥胖、糖尿病和心脏病的高发病率。根据世界卫生组织的数据，80% 的心脏病和中风死亡病例是由高血压、吸烟、胆固醇升高以及水果和蔬菜摄入不足引起的。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. “It’s a different paradigm(范式) of how to treat disease,” says Dr. Brenda Rea, who helps run the family and preventive medicine residency program at Loma Linda University School of Medicine. The lifestyle medicine specialty is designed to train doctors in how to prevent and treat disease, in part, by changing patients’ nutritional habits. The medical center and school at Loma Linda also has a food cupboard and kitchen for patients. This way, patients not only learn about which foods to buy, but also how to prepare them at home.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. “这是一种不同的治疗疾病的范例，”布伦达·雷博士说，她帮助管理洛马琳达大学医学院的家庭和预防医学住院医师项目。生活方式医学专业旨在培训医生如何通过改变患者的营养习惯来预防和治疗疾病。洛马琳达的医疗中心和学校还为患者提供食品柜和厨房。这样，患者不仅了解要购买哪些食物，还了解如何在家准备食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Many people don’t know how to cook, Rea says, and they only know how to heat things up. That means depending on packaged food with high salt and sugar content. So teaching people about which foods are healthy and how to prepare them, she says, can actually transform a patient’s life. And beyond that, it might transform the health and lives of that patient’s family. “What people eat can be medicine or poison,” Rea says. “As a physician, nutrition is one of the most powerful things you can change to reverse the effects of long-term disease.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I. 许多人不知道如何做饭，Rea 说，他们只知道如何加热食物。这意味着依赖高盐和高糖含量的包装食品。因此，她说，教导人们哪些食物是健康的以及如何准备它们，实际上可以改变患者的生活。除此之外，它可能会改变患者家人的健康和生活。 “人们吃的东西可能是药物，也可能是毒药，”雷亚说。 “作为一名医生，营养是你可以改变以扭转长期疾病影响的最有力的东西之一。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J. Studies have explored evidence that dietary changes can slow inflammation(炎症), for example, or make the body inhospitable to cancer cells. In general, many lifestyle medicine physicians recommend a plant-based diet — particularly for people with diabetes or other inflammatory conditions.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 研究已经探索了饮食变化可以减缓炎症的证据，例如，或者使身体不适合癌细胞。一般来说，许多生活方式医学医生推荐植物性饮食——特别是对于患有糖尿病或其他炎症性疾病的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. “As what happened with tobacco, this will require a cultural shift, but that can happen,” says Nguyen. “In the same way physicians used to smoke, and then stopped smoking and were able to talk to patients about it, I think physicians can have a bigger voice in it.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K. Nguyen 说：“正如烟草行业所发生的情况一样，这需要文化转变，但这可能会发生。” “就像医生过去吸烟，然后戒烟并能够与患者谈论吸烟一样，我认为医生可以在这方面拥有更大的发言权。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. More than half of the food Americans eat is factory-produced.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 美国人吃的食物一半以上是工厂生产的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. There is a special program that assigns doctors to give advice to shoppers in food stores.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 有一个特别计划指派医生向食品店的购物者提供建议。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. There is growing evidence from research that food helps patients recover from various illnesses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 越来越多的研究证据表明，食物有助于患者从各种疾病中康复。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. A healthy breakfast can be prepared quickly and easily.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 可以快速、轻松地准备健康的早餐。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Training a patient to prepare healthy food can change their life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 训练病人准备健康食物可以改变他们的生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. One food-as-medicine program not only prescribes food for treatment but teaches patients how to cook it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 一项以食为药的计划不仅开具治疗用食物，还教患者如何烹饪。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Scott is not keen on cooking food herself, thinking it would simply be a waste of time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 斯科特不热衷于自己做饭，认为这只是浪费时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Diabetes patients are advised to eat more plant-based food.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 建议糖尿病患者多吃植物性食物。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Using food as medicine is no novel idea, but the movement is making headway these days.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 用食物作为药物并不是什么新鲜想法，但近年来这一运动正在取得进展。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Americans’ high rates of various illnesses result from the way they eat.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 美国人患各种疾病的高比率是由他们的饮食方式造成的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 and 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 46 和 50 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: California has been facing a drought for many years now, with certain areas even having to pump freshwater hundreds of miles to their distribution system. The problem is growing as the population of the state continues to expand. New research has found deep water reserves under the state which could help solve their drought crisis. Previous drilling of wells could only reach depths of 1,000 feet, but due to new pumping practices, water deeper than this can now be extracted (抽取). The team at Stanford investigated the aquifers(地下蓄水层)below this depth and found that reserves may be triple what was previously thought.
paragraphs.translationZh: 加州多年来一直面临干旱，某些地区甚至不得不将淡水泵送到数百英里之外的配水系统。随着该州人口的不断增长，这个问题日益严重。新的研究发现该州的深水储备可以帮助解决干旱危机。以前的井钻探只能达到 1,000 英尺的深度，但由于新的抽水方法，现在可以提取（抽取）比此更深的水。斯坦福大学的研究小组调查了这个深度以下的地下蓄水层，发现储量可能是之前认为的三倍。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is profitable to drill to depths more than 1,000 feet for oil and gas extraction, but only recently in California has it become profitable to pump water from this depth. The aquifers range from 1,000 to 3,000 feet below the ground, which means that pumping will be expensive and there are other concerns. The biggest concern of pumping out water from this deep in the gradual settling down of the land surface. As the water is pumped out, the vacant space left is compacted by the weight of the earth above.
paragraphs.translationZh: 钻探超过 1,000 英尺的深度进行石油和天然气开采是有利可图的，但直到最近在加利福尼亚州，从这个深度抽水才变得有利可图。含水层位于地下 1,000 至 3,000 英尺之间，这意味着抽水成本高昂，而且还存在其他问题。从这个深处抽出水的最大问题是地表逐渐沉降。当水被抽出时，剩下的空余空间被上面的地球重量压实。

paragraphs.sourceText: Even though pumping from these depths is expensive, it is still cheaper than desalinating(脱盐)the ocean water in the largely coastal state. Some desalination plants exist where feasible, but they are costly to run and can need constant repairs. Wells are much more reliable sources of freshwater, and California is hoping that these deep wells may be the answer to their severe water shortage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管从这些深度抽水的成本很高，但它仍然比在主要沿海国家淡化海水便宜。在可行的情况下存在一些海水淡化厂，但它们的运营成本很高，并且需要不断维修。水井是更可靠的淡水来源，加州希望这些深井能够解决其严重的水资源短缺问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: One problem with these sources is that the deep water also has a higher level of salt than shallower aquifers. This means that some wells may even need to undergo desalination after extraction, thus increasing the cost. Research from the exhaustive study of groundwater from over 950 drilling logs has just been published. New estimates of the water reserves now go up to 2,700 billion cubic meters of freshwater.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些来源的一个问题是深水的盐含量也高于浅层含水层。这意味着有些井在开采后甚至可能需要进行海水淡化，从而增加了成本。对超过 950 份钻井日志的地下水进行详尽研究的研究刚刚发表。新估计的淡水储量现已达到 2.7 万亿立方米。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The AlphaGo program’s victory is an example of how smart computers have become.
paragraphs.translationZh: AlphaGo 程序的胜利是计算机变得智能的一个例子。

paragraphs.sourceText: But can artificial intelligence (AI) machines act ethically, meaning can they be honest and fair?
paragraphs.translationZh: 但人工智能 (AI) 机器的行为是否符合道德规范，即它们能否诚实和公平？

paragraphs.sourceText: One example of AI is driverless cars. They are already on California roads, so it is not too soon to ask whether we can program a machine to act ethically. As driverless cars improve, they will save lives. They will make fewer mistakes than human drivers do. Sometimes, however, they will face a choice between lives. Should the cars be programmed to avoid hitting a child running across the road, even if that will put their passengers at risk? What about making a sudden turn to avoid a dog? What if the only risk is damage to the car itself, not to the passengers?
paragraphs.translationZh: 人工智能的一个例子是无人驾驶汽车。它们已经在加州的道路上行驶，所以现在问我们是否可以对机器进行编程以使其行为符合道德还为时过早。随着无人驾驶汽车的改进，它们将拯救生命。他们比人类司机犯的错误更少。然而，有时他们会面临人生的选择。是否应该对汽车进行编程以避免撞到跑过马路的儿童，即使这会让乘客面临危险？突然转弯躲避狗怎么样？如果唯一的风险是汽车本身损坏，而不是乘客损坏怎么办？

paragraphs.sourceText: Perhaps there will be lessons to learn from driverless cars, but they are not super-intelligent beings. Teaching ethics to a machine even more intelligent than we are will be the bigger challenge.
paragraphs.translationZh: 也许我们可以从无人驾驶汽车中吸取教训，但它们并不是超级智能生物。向比我们更聪明的机器教授道德将是更大的挑战。

paragraphs.sourceText: About the same time as AlphaGo’s triumph, Microsoft’s ‘chatbot’ took a bad turn. The software, named Taylor, was designed to answer messages from people aged 18-24. Taylor was supposed to be able to learn from the messages she received. She was designed to slowly improve her ability to handle conversations, but some people were teaching Taylor racist ideas. When she started saying nice things about Hitler, Microsoft turned her off and deleted her ugliest messages.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大约在 AlphaGo 获胜的同时，微软的“聊天机器人”也发生了糟糕的转变。该软件名为 Taylor，旨在回复 18 至 24 岁人群的消息。泰勒应该能够从她收到的消息中学习。她的目的是慢慢提高她处理对话的能力，但有些人正在向泰勒传授种族主义思想。当她开始说希特勒的好话时，微软将她拒之门外，并删除了她最丑陋的消息。

paragraphs.sourceText: AlphaGo’s victory and Taylor’s defeat happened at about the same time. This should be a warning to us. It is one thing to use AI within a game with clear rules and clear goals. It is something very different to use AI in the real world. The unpredictability of the real world may bring to the surface a troubling software problem.
paragraphs.translationZh: AlphaGo的胜利和泰勒的失败几乎同时发生。这对我们应该是一个警告。在规则明确、目标明确的游戏中使用人工智能是一回事。在现实世界中使用人工智能是非常不同的。现实世界的不可预测性可能会使令人不安的软件问题浮出水面。

paragraphs.sourceText: Eric Schmidt is one of the bosses of Google, which own AlphoGo. He thinks AI will be positive for humans. He said people will be the winner, whatever the outcome. Advances in AI will make human beings smarter, more able and “just better human beings.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 埃里克·施密特是谷歌的老板之一，该公司拥有 AlphoGo。他认为人工智能将为人类带来积极的影响。他说，无论结果如何，人们都会成为赢家。人工智能的进步将使人类变得更聪明、更有能力、“成为更好的人类”。
